jp: このカレー屋[や]は安[やす]くておいしいと聞[き]きました。{それなのに|cn-sorenanoni}、お客[きゃく]さんが一人[ひとり]もいません。
en: I heard this curry shop is cheap and tasty. And yet there is not a single customer.
why: Empty seats go against what a cheap, tasty shop leads you to expect, so a 'despite that' connector is needed.

jp: 財布[さいふ]の中[なか]にはお金[かね]があまりありません。{それでも|cn-sorenanoni}、友達[ともだち]の誕生日[たんじょうび]プレゼントを買[か]いたいです。
en: I do not have much money in my wallet. Even so, I want to buy my friend a birthday present.
why: The wish holds in spite of the lack of money; だから would wrongly make poverty the reason for buying.

jp: 毎月[まいつき]貯金[ちょきん]しています。{それなのに/それでも|cn-sorenanoni}、お金[かね]がなかなか貯[た]まりません。
en: I save money every month. And yet the money hardly builds up.
why: Saving should make money accumulate, so the opposite outcome is introduced by a 'despite that' connector.

jp: この店[みせ]の弁当[べんとう]は高[たか]いです。{それでも/それなのに|cn-sorenanoni}、いつも昼[ひる]までに売[う]り切[き]れてしまいます。
en: The lunch boxes at this shop are expensive. Even so, they always sell out by noon.
why: Selling out goes against what a high price suggests; だから would turn the price into a reason for selling well.

jp: 値段[ねだん]が高[たか]い{にもかかわらず|cn-sorenanoni}、このバッグはよく売[う]れています。
en: Despite the high price, this bag sells well.
why: Selling well goes against a high price, so にもかかわらず ('despite') attaches to the plain form 高い.

jp: 雨[あめ]の日[ひ]{にもかかわらず|cn-sorenanoni}、市場[いちば]は買[か]い物客[ものきゃく]でいっぱいでした。
en: Despite it being a rainy day, the market was full of shoppers.
why: A crowded market goes against rain, so noun + にもかかわらず ('despite') is needed.

jp: レシートをなくしてしまいました。{それでも|cn-sorenanoni}、店員[てんいん]さんは親切[しんせつ]に返品[へんぴん]を受[う]け付[つ]けてくれました。
en: I had lost the receipt. Even so, the clerk kindly accepted the return.
why: Accepting the return goes against the missing receipt; だから would wrongly make the lost receipt its cause.

jp: 昨日[きのう]は五千円[ごせんえん]も使[つか]いました。{それなのに/それでも|cn-sorenanoni}、欲[ほ]しかった物[もの]は何[なに]も買[か]えませんでした。
en: I spent as much as five thousand yen yesterday. And yet I could not buy anything I wanted.
why: Spending that much should have bought something; the empty result is a complaint, which それなのに expresses.

jp: 給料日[きゅうりょうび]の前[まえ]でお金[かね]がありません。{それでも|cn-sorenanoni}、友達[ともだち]との食事[しょくじ]には行[い]くつもりです。
en: It is just before payday and I have no money. Even so, I intend to go out for a meal with my friends.
why: The intention stands in spite of having no money, so a 'despite that' connector fits, not a result connector.

jp: 店員[てんいん]さんに三回[さんかい]も確認[かくにん]しました。{それなのに/それでも|cn-sorenanoni}、注文[ちゅうもん]した物[もの]と違[ちが]う料理[りょうり]が来[き]ました。
en: I checked with the waiter three times. And yet a different dish from the one I ordered arrived.
why: After repeated checking you expect the right dish, so the wrong one is introduced with the complaining それなのに.

jp: 店員[てんいん]さんは「これ以上[いじょう]は安[やす]くできません」と言[い]いました。{それでも|cn-sorenanoni}、私[わたし]は値引[ねび]きをお願[ねが]いし続[つづ]けました。
en: The clerk said, "I can't go any lower than this." Even so, I kept asking for a discount.
why: The speaker keeps asking despite the refusal; だから would make the refusal the reason for asking.

jp: 彼[かれ]は大[おお]きな借金[しゃっきん]があります。{それなのに/それでも|cn-sorenanoni}、毎晩[まいばん]高[たか]い店[みせ]で食事[しょくじ]をしています。
en: He has a large debt. And yet he eats at expensive restaurants every night.
why: Eating out expensively goes against having a large debt, so a 'despite that' connector is needed.

jp: 物価[ぶっか]が上[あ]がっています。{それでも|cn-sorenanoni}、この町[まち]のパン屋[や]は昔[むかし]の値段[ねだん]を守[まも]っています。
en: Prices are going up. Even so, the bakery in this town is keeping its old prices.
why: Keeping old prices goes against rising prices in general, which それでも marks; だから would give a false cause.

jp: 不景気[ふけいき]{にもかかわらず|cn-sorenanoni}、あの店[みせ]は毎年[まいとし]売[う]り上[あ]げを伸[の]ばしています。
en: Despite the recession, that shop increases its sales every year.
why: Growing sales run against a recession, so noun + にもかかわらず ('despite') is the right form.
